src/app.module.ts.reason: ADR 0010 D9, no domain seam: the root module lists every feature module and sub-module in the order Nest registers their routes (route-order.test.ts replays it), and a parent module never imports its sub-modules (D3), so no feature module can hold a share of the list. Its max rises with each module added: that commit carries the Architecture-Debt trailer for this file and needs no other reason.

src/bus/config/bus-config.mapper.ts.reason: ADR 0010 D9, no domain seam: toBusGroups is the bus list as one ordered literal per group (hssc, campus, fasttrack, commute, then each Jongro route), and each group's field order is the ETag input; the realtime and schedule groups share the card, badge and station helpers, so a sub-module would hold group builders and nothing else.

src/bus/stops/bus-stops.rules.ts.reason: ADR 0010 D9, no domain seam: schedule-stops.json is one operator-edited document, and its boot failure lists every issue in the words bus-stops.rules.spec.ts pins. The checks (stops, photos, panoramas, guides, sequences, estimate opt-ins) compose into the one validator the schema runs, and child-to-parent imports keep a sub-module from holding a piece of it. docs/plans/private-file tracks the zod rewrite that retires this entry.

src/map/layer-set/map-layer-set.rules.ts.reason: ADR 0010 D9, no domain seam: the layer-set file is one operator-edited document, and its schema composes these checks (chips, lists, option windows, cross-references). Child-to-parent imports put a zod composite's leaves above it, so a sub-module split cannot hold them, and the leaves alone exceed the rules cap.

src/map/layer-set/map-layer-set.schema.t.reason: ADR 0010 D9, no domain seam: layerSetFile is one zod composite over one operator-edited document. src/notices/list/notices-list.rules.ts.reason: ADR 0010 D9, no domain seam: the list badge is one priority chain a list item is cut from, the v1 period pick and the v2 role badge feeding one brief, and the cursor decode beside it; neither half is a flow of its own, so a sub-module would hold rules and nothing else, and the badge alone exceeds the rules cap.
